subject.title: Telegram owner commands: trusted execution mode for approval-gated actions

question: Should OpenClaw add a trusted-owner approval-bypass mode for Telegram group-origin privileged actions, and should that policy live in a shared approval layer rather than a Telegram-only config key?
rationale: The request intentionally skips approval prompts for privileged group-chat actions based on Telegram identity and group trust, which changes a security boundary and adds config surface that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design Shared Trusted-Owner Policy
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the approval stack.

options.title: Keep Current Approval Model
options.body: Decline the bypass and document elevated/full plus full/off host approvals as the supported no-prompt operator workflow.

options.title: Add Telegram-Only Shortcut
options.body: Implement a narrow Telegram setting, accepting faster ergonomics but higher risk of policy drift from shared approvals and elevated execution.

recommendation.title: Design Shared Trusted-Owner Policy
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the approval stack.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a product/security boundary choice, with implementation routing to Telegram and approval owners after direction is set.
